site_subset_labels: Overlapping lesion of retroperitoneum and peritoneum
rationale: Invasive implants of ovarian serous borderline tumors are, by definition, epithelial proliferations located on/within the peritoneal surface; WHO 2014 reclassified them as peritoneal involvement (low-grade serous carcinoma), so the entity is restricted to the peritoneum within its ceiling.
source_name: PubMed PMC5298321 (Virchows Archiv, Ovarian borderline tumors in the 2014 WHO classification)

rationale: Low-grade serous carcinoma is a multi-site serous entity occurring across ovary, fallopian tube, peritoneum, uterus and cervix, covering essentially the full female-genital/peritoneal ceiling rather than a defined proper subset.
source_name: Wikipedia / WHO serous carcinoma one-entity concept

rationale: Micropapillary serous carcinoma is a serous carcinoma pattern occurring across ovary, tube, peritoneum and other female-genital sites; it is not restricted to a defined proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Johns Hopkins (ovarian serous borderline tumors review)

rationale: High-grade serous carcinoma is a multi-site serous entity of ovary, fallopian tube, peritoneum, uterus and cervix, spanning essentially the full female-genital/peritoneal ceiling rather than a proper subset.
source_name: Wikipedia / WHO serous carcinoma one-entity concept

term: Primary serous papillary carcinoma of peritoneum
site_subset_labels: Overlapping lesion of retroperitoneum and peritoneum
rationale: By definition this is a primary peritoneal tumor arising from the peritoneal lining, diagnosed only when the ovaries are uninvolved, so it is restricted to the peritoneum within its ceiling.

HPV-independent gastric-type adenocarcinoma is a defined tumor of the uterine cervix (with documented vaginal counterparts), not an established primary of ovary, fallopian tube or endometrium, so it is restricted to the cervix/vagina subset of the ceiling.
source_name: PubMed PMC11075765 (Gastric-type adenocarcinoma of the uterine cervix)

rationale: The descriptor 'endocervical type' defines this mucinous adenocarcinoma as a cervical (endocervical) entity, restricting it to the cervix codes within the ceiling.
source_name: PubMed PMC11075765 (Gastric-type adenocarcinoma of the uterine cervix)

rationale: Gastric-type mucinous carcinoma is a defined tumor of the uterine cervix (with reported vaginal cases), not an established ovarian, tubal or endometrial primary, restricting it to the cervix/vagina subset of the ceiling.
source_name: PubMed PMC11075765 (Gastric-type adenocarcinoma of the uterine cervix)

rationale: HPV-associated adenocarcinoma in situ is a preinvasive glandular lesion of the uterine (endo)cervix, restricting it to the cervix codes within the ceiling rather than other female-genital sites.
Cervical glandular intraepithelial neoplasia (CGIN) is by definition a glandular preinvasive lesion of the cervix, restricting it to the cervix codes within the ceiling.
source_name: North Tees & Hartlepool NHS (Glandular abnormalities of the cervix)

rationale: HPV-independent (gastric-type) adenocarcinoma in situ is a recognized preinvasive glandular lesion of the uterine cervix, restricting it to the cervix codes within the ceiling.
source_name: MyPathologyReport (Adenocarcinoma in situ of the cervix)

rationale: Atypical lobular endocervical glandular hyperplasia is a precursor lesion of gastric-type adenocarcinoma arising in the uterine cervix (endocervical glands), restricting it to the cervix codes within the ceiling.
source_name: PubMed PMC10728631 (Atypical lobular endocervical glandular hyperplasia)

term: Gastric-type adenocarcinoma in situ of cervix
rationale: The term explicitly names a gastric-type adenocarcinoma in situ 'of cervix', a preinvasive cervical glandular lesion, restricting it to the cervix codes within the ceiling.

HPV-independent adenocarcinoma (NOS) is defined in WHO as an HPV-independent cervical adenocarcinoma category, restricting it to the cervix codes within the ceiling rather than other female-genital sites.
source_name: MyPathologyReport (Adenocarcinoma in situ of the cervix)

rationale: Myxoid leiomyosarcoma is a smooth-muscle sarcoma arising at many anatomic sites (uterus, soft tissue, viscera, etc.), so it is not restricted to a defined proper subset of its broad ceiling.

Endometrial/endometrial stromal sarcoma arises in the uterine corpus and cervix and rarely at extrauterine sites (peritoneum, ovary) via endometriosis, covering essentially the ceiling sites rather than a proper subset.

Endometrial stromal sarcoma occurs in the uterine corpus and cervix and, rarely, extrauterine sites (peritoneum, ovary) associated with endometriosis, matching essentially the full ceiling rather than a proper subset.
High-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma arises in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely at extrauterine sites via endometriosis, covering essentially the ceiling rather than a proper subset.

Endometrioid (endometrial) stromal sarcoma, high-grade, arises in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely at extrauterine endometriosis-associated sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
High-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma occurs in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely at extrauterine endometriosis-associated sites, covering essentially the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
High-grade endometrioid stromal sarcoma arises in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely extrauterine endometriosis-associated sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.

Endolymphatic stromal myosis is a synonym of low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma, occurring in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely extrauterine endometriosis-associated sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma arises in the uterine corpus (more than cervix) and rarely extrauterine sites via endometriosis, covering essentially the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Endometrial stromatosis is a synonym of low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma, arising in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely extrauterine sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Low-grade endometrioid (endometrial) stromal sarcoma arises in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely extrauterine endometriosis-associated sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma arises in the uterine corpus (more than cervix) and rarely extrauterine sites via endometriosis, covering essentially the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Low-grade endometrioid stromal sarcoma arises in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely extrauterine endometriosis-associated sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.

Stromal endometriosis is used synonymously for low-grade endometrial stromal proliferations arising in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely extrauterine sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.

Stromal myosis (endolymphatic stromal myosis) is a synonym of low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma occurring in the uterine corpus/cervix and rarely extrauterine sites, matching the ceiling rather than a proper subset.

Müllerian adenosarcoma arises across multiple female-genital sites (uterus, cervix, ovary, fallopian tube, vagina, and extrauterine peritoneal sites), covering essentially the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Adenosarcoma with stromal overgrowth is a variant of Müllerian adenosarcoma occurring across multiple female-genital sites, not restricted to a defined proper subset of the ceiling.
Müllerian adenosarcoma arises across multiple female-genital sites (uterus, cervix, ovary, tube, vagina, peritoneum), covering essentially the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Mesodermal (Müllerian) adenosarcoma occurs across multiple female-genital sites, not restricted to a defined proper subset of the ceiling.
Müllerian adenosarcoma arises across multiple female-genital sites (uterus, cervix, ovary, tube, vagina, peritoneum), covering essentially the ceiling rather than a proper subset.
Müllerian mixed tumor (carcinosarcoma) arises across female-genital sites (uterus, ovary, cervix, fallopian tube) and peritoneum, covering essentially the ceiling rather than a defined proper subset.
source_name: General gynecologic pathology (Müllerian mixed tumor multi-site)

rationale: Mesodermal mixed tumor (carcinosarcoma) arises across female-genital sites (cervix, uterus, ovary, tube) and peritoneum, covering essentially the ceiling rather than a defined proper subset.
source_name: General gynecologic pathology (mesodermal mixed tumor multi-site)

rationale: Malignant serous adenofibroma is a serous adenofibromatous carcinoma that arises in both the ovary and fallopian tube, the only two sites in its ceiling, so no proper subset restriction applies.
Malignant serous cystadenofibroma is a serous cystadenofibromatous carcinoma of the ovary and fallopian tube, the only two ceiling sites, so no proper subset restriction applies.
Serous adenocarcinofibroma is a serous carcinoma arising in a serous adenofibroma of the ovary or fallopian tube, the only two ceiling sites, so no proper subset restriction applies.
Serous cystadenocarcinofibroma is a serous carcinoma arising in a serous cystadenofibroma of the ovary or fallopian tube, the only two ceiling sites, so no proper subset restriction applies.
Diffuse mesothelioma (NOS) can arise from any serosal surface (pleura, peritoneum, tunica vaginalis), spanning multiple ceiling sites rather than a defined proper subset.
Diffuse pleural mesothelioma originates specifically from the mesothelial cells of the parietal or visceral pleura, restricting it to the pleura (C384) within its ceiling.
Localized mesothelioma (NOS) can arise on any serosal surface (pleura, peritoneum, tunica vaginalis), spanning multiple ceiling sites rather than a defined proper subset.
source_name: Modern Pathology (Localized malignant mesothelioma of serosal origin)

rationale: Localized pleural mesothelioma arises specifically along the pleural surface, restricting it to the pleura (C384) within its ceiling.

Mesothelioma (NOS) is a generic mesothelial malignancy that can arise on any serosal surface (pleura, peritoneum, pericardium, tunica vaginalis), spanning multiple ceiling sites rather than a defined proper subset.
